What We Can Achieve Together:


The Contracts Manager serves as the contracts lead for the Northeast Division, providing leadership, oversight, and coordinated service delivery across the Division. The position also directly manages complex agreements and provides contract management, compliance, and stakeholder support for assigned Business Units and Division priorities.

Working closely with Project Managers, Program Managers, Award Managers, Finance, Grants, Operations, Legal, and Division leadership, the Contracts Manager provides expertise on agreement structures, contracting strategies, compliance requirements, and organizational policies. The position promotes consistent practices, coordinates priorities and workloads, develops staff capabilities, and leads process improvements that strengthen compliance, service delivery, and operational effectiveness.


The Contracts Manager administers and oversees contract management activities for the Northeast Division, ensuring agreements are developed, reviewed, executed, monitored, and closed in accordance with organizational policies, Delegation of Authority requirements, and risk management practices. The manager serves as an expert resource on contract administration, compliance requirements, and contracting best practices, providing guidance to staff and stakeholders on complex agreements and contractual matters. The role partners with Legal, Finance, Grants, Operations, and program staff to support effective contract management, resolve contract-related issues, strengthen organizational compliance, and advance continuous improvement efforts across the Division.


RESPONSIBILITIES & SCOPE

  • Leads contract management services across the Northeast Division, establishing priorities, coordinating workloads, monitoring service delivery, and promoting timely, consistent, and compliant support across Business Units and Division priorities.
  • Maintains oversight of the Division's contract portfolio and contract service delivery, identifying emerging workload, compliance, and risk issues and recommending appropriate resource or service-delivery adjustments.
  • Serves as the divisional subject matter expert and escalation point for complex contracting matters, providing guidance on agreement structures, compliance requirements, risk considerations, organizational policies, and contracting best practices.
  • Evaluates contractual, financial, compliance, operational, and reputational risks; recommends mitigation strategies; and escalates significant or unresolved matters to the appropriate organizational leaders and subject matter experts.
  • Partners with Legal, Finance, Grants, Operations, program staff, and other stakeholders to resolve contract-related issues, mitigate risk, and support organizational objectives.
  • Supervises, coaches, and develops contracts staff and provides functional guidance to others with contracting responsibilities, building capacity and fostering collaboration, accountability, customer service, and continuous improvement.
  • Leads the development and implementation of processes, tools, training, service standards, and resources that improve compliance, operational effectiveness, and the stakeholder experience.
  • Exercises significant independent judgment in resolving complex contract issues, prioritizing competing demands, allocating resources, and recommending solutions that balance organizational objectives with legal, financial, operational, and reputational risk.

We’re Looking for You:


Are you looking for work you can believe in? At TNC we strive to embody a philosophy of Work that You Can Believe in where you can feel like you are making a difference every day. We’re looking for someone with strong experience in leading a diverse, multi-disciplinary team. The ideal candidate should have exceptional communication and collaboration skills and experience in management of controls and reports of a business unit. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the ongoing mission of conservation by directing and shaping the work of our team!


What You’ll Bring:


  • Bachelor's Degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration or related field and 4 years' related experience or equivalent combination.
  • Experience with government regulations related to grants and contracts.
  • TNC Certified Contract Specialist (CCS) certification or ability to obtain certification within established timeframes.
  • Experience managing contracts, agreements, procurement activities, grants, or related business operations.
  • Experience coordinating multiple agreements and managing competing priorities simultaneously.
  • Experience interpreting and applying organizational policies, procedures, compliance requirements, and approval processes.
  • Experience using contract management systems, document management systems, financial systems, or related technology platforms.
  • Experience supervising, coaching, and developing staff. 

Desired Qualifications:


  • Experience managing complex contracts, subawards, procurement agreements, professional services agreements, or other organizational agreements.
  • Experience supporting contracts funded by government, foundation, corporate, or other institutional sources.
  • Knowledge of contract lifecycle management, procurement practices, internal controls, compliance monitoring, and risk management.
  • Experience supervising and developing staff or leading a contracts, procurement, grants, or related service-delivery function.
  • Experience designing or improving contracting processes, tools, templates, training, and service standards.
  • Experience working collaboratively with Legal, Finance, Grants, Operations, and program teams in a complex or decentralized organization.
  • Strong analytical, judgment, problem-solving, project-management, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex requirements clearly to varied audiences.
  • Experience using contract lifecycle management, financial, procurement, or document-management systems.
  • Multi-lingual skills and/or multi-cultural experience appreciated.

Salary Information:


The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $77,860 - $103,785. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate's location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Please note countries outside the USA would have a different pay range in the local currency based on the local labor market, and not tied to USA pay or ranges. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment.

Who We Are:

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring:

Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports of the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

Employees must submit their application by logging into Workday and applying via the Jobs Hub.

The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer.Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law.

The successful applicant must meet the requirements of The Nature Conservancy's background screening process.

Do you have military experience? Visit our U.S. Military Skills Translator to match your military experience with our current job openings!

TNC is committed to offering accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please send a note to with Request for Accommodation in the subject line.

Are you ready to accelerate your potential and make a real difference within life sciences, diagnostics and biotechnology?

At Cytiva, one of Danaher’s 15+ operating companies, our work saves lives—and we’re all united by a shared commitment to innovate for tangible impact.

You’ll thrive in a culture of belonging where you and your unique viewpoint matter. And by harnessing Danaher’s system of continuous improvement, you help turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life.

Working at Cytiva means being at the forefront of providing new solutions to transform human health. Our incredible customers undertake life-saving activities ranging from fundamental biological research to developing innovative vaccines, new medicines, and cell and gene therapies.

At Cytiva you will be able to continuously improve yourself and us – working on challenges that truly matter with people that care for each other, our customers, and their patients. Take your next step to an altogether life-changing career.

Learn about the Danaher Business System which makes everything possible.

The StrategicColumn Packing Specialist is responsible for delivering Cytiva's expert-led column packing service across the full scale spectrum — from lab and pilot-scale screening columns through to process-scale GMP columns — ensuring reproducible, specification-compliant packed beds throughout the customer's development-to-manufacturing journey.

By supporting customers at the resin screening and process development stage as well as at commercial manufacturing, this role builds early technical influence and secures resin and column design-in. It delivers expert-assured reproducibility, increased process uptime and consistent confidence in packed bed performance for customers running GMP production.

This position reports to the BioProcess Hardware Modality Leader, Korea and is part of the Bioprocessing organization located in Korea, working remotely to cover customers across Korea.

What you will do:

  • Execute column packing and unpacking across all scales:

- Lab / development scale — Tricorn, HiScale, XK and comparable columns supporting customer resin screening, method development and process development activities.

- Pilot scale — AxiChrom 50–200 mm, BPG, Fineline and equivalent columns.

- Process scale — AxiChrom and Chromaflow columns at customer GMP sites.

  • Qualify packed beds against agreed acceptance criteria (HETP, asymmetry), document results, and issue packing reports that customers can use as part of their manufacturing records.
  • Support customer resin screening and process development activities by packing small-scale columns to consistent, documented specifications — enabling reliable scale-down model performance and generating packing data that supports subsequent scale-up.
  • Provide focused support for strategic customers by prioritizing high-impact accounts, aligning technical service activities with commercial priorities, and ensuring responsive, expert-led support for critical development, scale-up and manufacturing needs.
  • Support customer issues involving the interaction between resin and columns, including troubleshooting performance deviations, packed-bed behavior, resin handling, column hardware conditions and scale-related issues in collaboration with modality, application and global technical teams.
  • Ensure scale-up consistency by translating packing parameters established at lab and pilot scale (compression factor, packing flow velocity, bed height) into validated process-scale packing methods, and by advising customers on the scale-up implications of resin and column selection.
  • Train and certify customer operators across scales — covering lab-scale packing technique for process development groups, and process-scale packing, unpacking, CIP and routine handling for manufacturing operators — at customer sites and demo centers.
  • Act as technical escalation point for packing-related issues, engaging global product, R&D, quality and service teams to investigate and close complex cases such as bed instability, channeling, repeat repacking and resin damage.

Who you are:

  • Bachelor's degree or above in Biotechnology, Biochemical / Chemical Engineering, Life Sciences, Biochemistry or a related discipline.
  • Multiple years of hands-on experience in bioprocess downstream operations, with direct experience packing chromatography columns at both laboratory / pilot scale and process scale.
  • Practical understanding of chromatography resin properties, slurry preparation, compression / packing factors, and packed-bed evaluation methods (HETP, asymmetry, transition analysis), and how these translate across scales.
  • Demonstrated capability in customer-facing technical support, hands-on service delivery or field service within a bioprocessing or equivalent GMP-regulated environment.
  • Working knowledge of ÄKTA pure / pilot / process systems and UNICORN control software, sufficient to execute packing and evaluation runs independently on-site.
  • Fluent level of English and Korean in written and verbal communication, able to interface with both Korean customers and Cytiva's global product and service teams.

Our portfolio includes hit titles like Treasure Party, which combines match-3 puzzle gameplay with a board game adventure for a vibrant treasure-hunting experience, and Sort Wizard, a fresh take on sorting puzzle mechanics that challenges and delights players. Both games are quickly building strong followings in their genres, offering fun, rewarding journeys for puzzle lovers and adventurers alike.

Our team is driven, playful and deeply committed to excellence and innovation. We work together to craft clever, visually stunning, and memorable experiences. PlayQ's environment values initiative, collaboration, and individual leadership to ensure that our mission is fulfilled.

Who You Are:

  • Proactive Achiever You consistently take the initiative to drive business results, supported by sound reasoning and detailed execution plans.
  • Growth Driver You champion company-wide success by relentlessly focusing on achieving results, understanding how your work impacts the entire organization, and pushing to make it 10% better every time. You continuously level yourself up and drive the business forward.
  • Solution Seeker Fueled by curiosity, you explore various ways to solve a problem. Every hard problem is an opportunity in disguise.
  • Team Builder You actively foster strong dynamics within and between teams, contributing to our collective success.
  • Resilient Leader You consistently approach your work with resilience and a steadfast passion for achievement of our goals despite challenges or setbacks.
  • Data-Driven Creator You leverage data to back intuition. Empirical creativity is your go-to. Imagination led, data validated.

Why you'll want to come to work:

Our Senior Motion Graphics Designer role offers the opportunity to directly shape PlayQ’s growth through high-quality, performance driven user acquisition creative.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role focused on creating motion graphics, editorial content, gameplay driven ads, and high volume creative iterations for paid media campaigns. You will work closely with Marketing Art and User Acquisition to turn creative direction and performance learnings into engaging short form ads.

Your work will contribute directly to PlayQ’s growth by creating strong hooks, clear gameplay stories, and modular creative assets that can be tested, optimized, resized, and scaled efficiently across advertising platforms.

Your Responsibilities:

  • Motion Design: Design and animate high-quality motion graphics for user acquisition, social, and digital marketing campaigns using typography, transitions, visual effects, gameplay assets, UI, and graphic design to create visually compelling advertising creatives.
  • Video Production: Edit gameplay capture, promotional footage, AI-generated content, voiceover, music, and sound effects into engaging short-form video ads that effectively communicate gameplay, features, rewards, and player motivations.
  • Creative Storytelling: Apply strong editorial principles including pacing, timing, rhythm, and visual storytelling to create compelling narratives, impactful opening hooks, and high-performing marketing creatives.
  • Creative Development: Produce both net-new creative concepts and high-volume iterations of existing ads, developing structured variations that test hooks, messaging, gameplay moments, pacing, visual treatments, ensuring that all creative decisions improve campaign performance
  • Performance Marketing: Create performance-driven video ads for major paid media platforms including Meta, Google, TikTok, YouTube, AppLovin, Moloco, and other digital advertising channels, leveraging user acquisition best practices and platform-specific requirements.
  • Production Efficiency: Build organized, modular After Effects projects and reusable creative templates that enable rapid iteration, efficient production workflows, and consistent creative quality across campaigns.
  • Creative Optimization: Adapt marketing assets into polished deliverables across multiple aspect ratios, formats, and advertising placements while maintaining visual consistency and production excellence.
  • Project Organization: Maintain well-structured project files, naming conventions, source assets, and deliverables to support scalable creative production and effective cross-functional collaboration.
  • AI-Enhanced Production: Leverage modern AI tools to accelerate ideation, content generation, editing, iteration, and creative adaptation while applying strong creative judgment to ensure quality, consistency, and brand alignment.
  • Industry Research: Stay current on mobile advertising trends, emerging creative technologies, social media formats, competitor creatives, and evolving user acquisition best practices to continuously improve creative effectiveness.
  • Collaboration: Partner closely with Creative Director, User Acquisition, Design, and cross-functional stakeholders to align on campaign objectives, share creative insights, and deliver high-performing marketing assets.

What you’ll bring to the team:

  • Experience: 5+ years of professional experience in motion graphics, video editing, digital advertising, or performance marketing creative, with experience producing user acquisition creatives for mobile games.
  • Portfolio: A strong portfolio demonstrating expertise in motion design, editorial storytelling, gameplay advertising, and short-form video production that showcases measurable creative quality and performance.
  • Expertise: Advanced proficiency in Adobe After Effects, strong proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro, Adobe Photoshop, and working knowledge of Adobe Illustrator, with the ability to execute polished motion graphics and video editing workflows.
  • Creative Skills: Deep understanding of animation principles, typography, composition, visual hierarchy, compositing, pacing, rhythm, storytelling, music editing, sound design, and audio synchronization as applied to performance marketing.
  • Production Ability: Proven ability to combine gameplay footage, UI elements, typography, visual effects, sound, and graphic design into engaging, performance-focused short-form advertising creatives.
  • Optimization Mindset: Experience creating both original concepts and high-volume creative iterations, with a strong understanding of user acquisition testing methodologies, hook strategies, performance marketing workflows, and creative optimization.
  • Technical Organization: Experience building organized, modular project files and reusable templates that support efficient production, rapid creative iteration, and scalable content development.
  • Platform Knowledge: Familiarity with paid media platforms including Meta, Google, TikTok, YouTube, AppLovin, Moloco, and other digital advertising ecosystems, along with an understanding of performance metrics such as CTR, CPI, ROAS, conversion, retention, and hook performance.
  • AI Proficiency: Experience integrating AI tools into modern creative production workflows, including platforms such as Adobe Firefly, Photoshop AI, ChatGPT, Claude, and other emerging AI technologies to enhance ideation, editing, production, and creative adaptation while maintaining high creative standards.
  • Collaboration: Excellent communication, organization, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to independently own creative projects from concept through final delivery.

Bonus Points:

  • Industry Experience: Experience creating user acquisition creative for match-3, puzzle, casual, or hybrid casual mobile games, with a strong understanding of mobile gaming audiences and advertising strategies.
  • Additional Creative Expertise: Experience producing App Store screenshots, promotional graphics, App Store Optimization (ASO) assets, or other marketing collateral supporting mobile game launches and growth.
  • Technical Skills: Familiarity with Unity or other gameplay capture tools, Cinema 4D, Blender, or other 3D software for asset preparation and compositing support, as well as motion graphics plugins such as Trapcode, Saber, Element 3D, or similar technologies.
  • AI & Emerging Technology: Experience using generative AI platforms such as Runway, Midjourney, and other advanced creative tools to support content production and innovation.
  • Performance Collaboration: Experience working directly with User Acquisition teams and applying campaign performance insights, creative testing results, and user behavior data to continuously improve future creative development.

Working at PlayQ:

  • Remote Work Environment. Work remotely from anywhere in Latin America, with the flexibility to structure your day around your location while collaborating closely with our HQ and global teams.
  • Meaningful ownership & impact. Take ownership of growth initiatives and directly influence the strategy, performance, and success of our games.
  • AI-powered tools. Access to company-provided AI tools and paid subscriptions to support creative work, experimentation, and productivity.
  • Flexible time off. Take the time you need to recharge and maintain a healthy balance while delivering against your goals.
  • Career growth & visibility. Work closely with senior leadership and have the opportunity to grow your scope and influence as the business and products scale.
  • Create incredible games—for a living! Because who doesn’t love games?

At PlayQ, we leverage competitive benchmarking data when setting each role’s base pay range. Individual base salary will be determined based on job-related factors which may include knowledge, skills, experience, scope of role, business need and geographic location.

If your skillset aligns with the requirements of this role, we will contact you through our official Applicant Tracking System (Greenhouse) or company email address (@playq.net). If you receive communication from a different domain, this communication is not from a legitimate representative of PlayQ.

raw.description:
Please Note: If you are a current Spin Master employee with access to Workday, apply to this job via the Workday application.

Are you a kid at heart looking to build a career with a leading global children's toy, entertainment and digital gaming company?

At Spin Master, our unwavering commitment to open mindedness, integrity and innovation is a great part of what has made us an industry leader. How do we stay ahead of the pack? By hiring the best and brightest minds—and that’s why we want you!

Job Description:

What will you work on?
As the Senior Data Protection & Governance Engineer, you will lead the deployment of our Microsoft-centric data security, access control, and compliance ecosystem. Serving as the primary architect and implementer for Microsoft Purview, you will build a robust data governance architecture from the ground up, translating complex business and regulatory requirements into automated, scalable security guardrails.

This role is a full-time contract position with the opportunity to convert to permanent role.

How will you create impact?

  • Implement and configure the Microsoft Purview Data Catalog to enable data discovery, lineage, and governance across the M365 ecosystem.

  • Design and deploy a data classification framework utilizing automated security labels, sensitivity labels, retention policies, and comprehensive Records Management lifecycles.

  • Engineer and deploy unified Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies and configure Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management (IRM) to detect and mitigate internal data threats.

  • Implement strict access guardrails leveraging Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) using Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access.

  • Build Power Automate solutions integrating with SharePoint and other M365 services to automate compliance workflows and governance triggers.

  • Partner with Legal, InfoSec, and business units to translate compliance policies into Purview configurations while driving structured onboarding and adoption activities.

What are your skills and experience?

  • Proven track record of end-to-end implementations of Microsoft Purview from scratch to production, including Information Protection, Insider Risk, Data Catalog, and Records Management.

  • Deep technical experience building SaaS DLP policies within M365 and implementing advanced identity controls (RBAC/ABAC) in Azure/Entra ID.

  • Strong development and scripting capabilities using Power Automate and PowerShell to connect triggers to SharePoint and M365 APIs.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical whiteboarding sessions and translate complex governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) requirements into platform configurations.

  • Working knowledge of global privacy and security frameworks, including ISO 27001, ISO 42001, GDPR, and CCPA.

  • Microsoft SC-400 (Information Protection Administrator) or other relevant Microsoft security certifications are considered a strong asset.

  • Experience with network DLP via Zscaler or PowerApps development is considered an asset.



The anticipated pay range for candidates who will work in Ontario is $62.50 to $72.11 Per Hour. The offered pay to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to years of experience within the job, years of experience within the required industry, education, etc. Spin Master Inc. is a multi-state employer, and this salary range may not reflect positions that work only in other states.

This job posting is tied to an open vacancy.

What you can expect from us:

Our mission is to Make Life More Fun with a vision to push the boundaries of innovation, creativity, and fun.

  • Growth and Career Opportunities

  • Flexible Work Hours

  • Innovation, Collaboration and Fun

  • Comprehensive Benefits

  • Other fun Perks!

What’s it like to work here?

Spin Master is a fast-paced, hands-on organization that provides many great opportunities for impactful decision-making; though our challenging start-up atmosphere isn’t for everyone, we have a proven record of opportunities for future advancement and internal transfers for our passionate and results driven team.

Everyone is welcome in our sandbox and we are committed to an accessible and inclusive hiring process that provides reasonable accommodation to all applicants.

Spin Master strives to create an accessible and inclusive application and selection process and is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodation to job applicants who may require provisions to participate in the recruitment, selection and/or assessment processes. Should you require an accommodation, please contact our Talent Acquisition team, by email at or by phone at 416 364-6002 and we will work with you to meet your accessibility needs.

Follow us on Instagram and Twitter @SpinMaster to stay up to date on Spin Master career opportunities.

We do appreciate all interest; however only those selected for interview will be contacted.

Hanwha Vision America (HVA), formerly known as Hanwha Techwin, is an affiliate of the Hanwha Group, a Fortune Global 500 company. HVA is an industry-leading provider of advanced network video surveillance products, including IP cameras, storage devices, and video management systems founded on world-class technologies. We offer end-to-end security solutions and have achieved global success across a wide range of industry verticals including retail, transportation, education, banking, healthcare, hospitality and airports.

Hanwha Vision America is seeking an NSI Strategic Account Manager (SAM) to lead the development and execution of strategic growth initiatives within assigned National Systems Integrator (NSI) accounts. This role serves as the primary corporate relationship owner responsible for driving executive alignment, technology adoption, revenue growth, field engagement, and long-term partnership development.

The NSI Strategic Account Manager acts as the bridge between Hanwha Vision corporate leadership and the NSI's national, regional, vertical, and branch organizations. Success in this role requires a combination of executive relationship management, strategic planning, business development, and cross-functional leadership.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Develop and execute strategic business plans that drive revenue growth, technology adoption, and market share expansion within assigned National Systems Integrator (NSI) accounts.
  • Build and maintain executive-level relationships with key stakeholders, serving as Hanwha Vision's primary strategic liaison.
  • Conduct Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) to assess performance, align priorities, remove barriers, and identify growth opportunities.
  • Drive year-over-year revenue growth through white-space identification, pipeline development, and joint end-user opportunity creation.
  • Collaborate with Hanwha Vision Regional Sales Teams to increase branch engagement, account penetration, and project wins.
  • Lead technology roadmap discussions and accelerate approval, commercialization, and adoption of Hanwha Vision products and solutions.
  • Develop and maintain account playbooks, relationship maps, and strategic growth plans to support long-term partnership success.
  • Partner with NSI marketing teams to execute co-marketing campaigns, MDF initiatives, events, and demand-generation activities that produce measurable business results.
  • Drive sales and technical enablement through training programs, certifications, competitive positioning, and field support resources.
  • Serve as the central coordination point between NSI leadership and Hanwha Vision sales, marketing, product management, technical services, and executive teams to ensure strategic alignment and execution.

Qualification:

  • Minimum 10+ years of experience in B2B sales and account management, ideally within the manufacturing and/or National Systems Integrator space.
  • Proven track record of exceeding sales targets and quotas, demonstrating strong negotiation and closing skills.
  • Strong understanding of the security industry
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, with fluency in a second language being a valuable asset (especially Korean or Spanish).
  • Proven ability to build and maintain strong, long-term relationships with senior executives and key decision-makers.
  • The ability to develop and implement strategic account plans to achieve client goals.
  • Strong analytical skills to identify client needs, anticipate challenges, and develop effective solutions.
  • Proficiency in CRM software, sales automation tools, and other relevant technology.
  • Ability to travel approximately 40% to 60% of the time. Travel includes customer headquarters visits, executive business reviews, industry events, trade shows, and Hanwha Vision corporate meetings.

Desirable Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Business, Marketing, Engineering, or related field.
  • Experience supporting large National Systems Integrators or Global Systems Integrators.
  • Knowledge of enterprise security deployments and technology approval processes.
  • Experience leading executive business reviews and strategic planning sessions.
  • Industry certifications and active participation in security industry organizations are a plus.

Physical Demands:

  • Sitting/Travel: The role requires extended periods of sitting, including time spent traveling by car or plane, attending meetings, and working on a laptop or mobile devices while in offices, client locations, or remote settings. The position also involves periods of standing and walking during client visits and events.

raw.title: Helpline Contact Center Supervisor
raw.excerpt: Health Resources in Action, Inc.  (HRiA) is a non-profit organization working to improve and reimagine public health.
raw.description:
Health Resources in Action, Inc. (HRiA) is a non-profit organization working to improve and reimagine public health. We connect, consult, and collaborate to solve complex challenges of access and equity in our health and social systems. Together with our partners, clients, and collaborators, we create actionable solutions so that all people can thrive.

In 1957, The Medical Foundation (TMF) was created to primarily fund biomedical research in Massachusetts. Since then, we’ve been on a journey of evolution. We changed our name to Health Resources in Action (HRiA) to reflect our impact in the field of public health. Today, HRiA works with individuals, organizations, and communities to drive a policy and systems change approach to advance health and racial equity.

HRiA seeks sustainable solutions for complex problems using an anti-racist approach. We aim to be adaptable and flexible in meeting clients and partners where they are, offering our decades of knowledge and resources to collectively realize our dream of equitable, sustainable health for all. The foundation of this work is centered on our values:

  • Health and racial equity by identifying and addressing the root causes of health inequities, intentionally working to shift narratives and power imbalances and disrupt all systems of oppression.
  • Leading with heart by demonstrating our passionate commitment to our work, continuously challenging ourselves with humility and vulnerability while pursuing and holding ourselves accountable to our mission.
  • Collaboration by intentionally and respectfully leading, partnering, and following to strengthen relationships, uplift different voices and build trust.
  • Innovation by driving toward new strategies, questioning norms, and continuously learning and evolving to support the needs of our clients and communities.

HRiA offers exciting, engaging, and challenging employment opportunities for facilitators, trainers, researchers, analysts, policy specialists, grant managers, and more. People come to HRiA because of our commitment to advancing health equity and inspiring work; they stay for our wonderful clients, partners, and dedicated and dynamic staff. With our growing portfolio of high-impact work, person-centered policies, and generous benefits, our team continually invests in making HRiA a great place to work. Our diverse staff of over 270 people hail from 30+ states, with a homebase in Boston’s Chinatown neighborhood.

As part of our Public Health Services, HRiA manages an extensive portfolio of behavioral health initiatives, including statewide substance use helplines in Vermont and Oregon and substance use and problem gambling helplines in Massachusetts and Illinois. The Illinois Helpline for Opioids and Other Substances (Illinois Department of Human Services, Division of Substance Use Prevention and Recovery) was launched in 2017, building upon our experience operating the MA Substance Use Helpline (Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Bureau of Substance Addiction Services) for over 23 years. HRiA launched the Vermont Helplink (Vermont Department of Health, Division of Substance Use Programs) in 2019. HRiA began operating the MA Problem Gambling Helpline (Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Office of Problem Gambling Services) in 2020 and the Illinois Problem Gambling Helpline (Illinois Department of Human Services, Division of Substance Use Prevention and Recovery) in 2022. In December 2023, HRiA launched the Oregon Recovery Center Hotline, now the Oregon Hopeline (Oregon Health Authority).

The Helpline contact center is the hub for the Helplines. Screening & Information Specialists (SIS) comprise most of the contact center team and respond to incoming Helpline inquiries. Four Contact Center Supervisors provide Helpline services and provide direct supervision to a portion of the SIS team. Three Masters-level Clinicians supervise a portion of the SIS, implement follow-up services, and provide additional coverage and support. Additional Helpline team members deliver and support program operations, marketing and communication, web management, and data analysis and management, supervision, and leadership. The larger team is overseen by the Managing Director, Behavioral Health.

To learn more about HRiA and our helplines, visit the following:

  • HRiA:
  • IL Problem Gambling Helpline:
  • MA Problem Gambling Helpline:
  • IL Helpline for Opioids and Other Substances:
  • VT Helplink: www.VTHelplink.org
  • MA Substance Use Helpline:
  • Oregon Hopeline:

Opportunity

We are seeking a full-time Helpline Contact Center Supervisor to join our team on the Oregon Recovery Center Hotline (Oregon Hopeline), Massachusetts Substance Use & Problem Gambling Helplines (MA Helpline), the Illinois Helpline for Opioids and Other Substances (IL Helpline), the Illinois Problem Gambling Helpline, and the Vermont Helplink (VT Helplink). This is an exciting opportunity to take on a newly developed position to support substance use treatment access across three states and supervise a diverse team of staff.

Position Description

We are seeking a full-time Helpline Contact Center Supervisor to join our team for the MA Helpines, the IL Helplines, and VT Helplink. We refer to these projects collectively as “the Helplines.” This is an exciting opportunity to support substance use treatment and problem gambling treatment access across three states and supervise a diverse team of staff.

The Contact Center Supervisors are responsible for handling incoming Helpline inquiries and providing supervisory support to the contact center team. A portion of their time is providing scheduled and as-needed Helpline coverage, in addition to our dedicated team of 22 Screening & Information Specialists (SIS). This includes responding to incoming calls, online chats, and SMS text messages from people seeking information about and help with accessing substance use and/or problem gambling services for themselves, a family member or friend, and/or a client. In this capacity, they assess Helpline users’ needs, determine the most appropriate substance use prevention, treatment, and/or recovery support service options, identify available options (through the Helplines’ databases), and refer callers to those services. They provide accurate information, education, support, and referrals in a non-judgmental, respectful, and culturally competent manner.

About half of their time, Contact Center Supervisors provide supervisory support to the SIS team. Each Supervisor acts as a shift supervisor for SIS while they are working. This includes monitoring SIS consumer interactions, consulting with SIS and intervening during difficult interactions, and addressing any urgent issues as well as supporting the social-emotional wellbeing of staff and fostering their skill-building and professional growth. The Contact Center Supervisor will provide on-going training to SIS through periodic in-service trainings on relevant topics and will assist in the onboarding of new SIS.

Each Supervisor also directly supervises up to six SIS team members. This includes providing bi-weekly supervision, processing timesheets, and assisting with schedule coordination. (SIS also receive regular, group-level supervision from one of our Clinicians.) Contact Center Supervisors are responsible for supporting contact center operations, including helping to coordinate a 24/7 coverage schedule, staffing, and technology needs. They are the liaisons between the contact center team and information technology (IT) support. The Contact Center Supervisor will also be called upon to contribute expertise to the development of policies, procedures, protocols, and curricula to support the Helplines, and may be engaged in providing this expertise to other HRiA teams and projects focused on substance use, problem gambling, and/or behavioral health equity.

This is a full-time, remote position with a salary range of $57,000 to $64,000 based on skills and experience. Supervisors will receive training to assess the needs of Helpline users, provide appropriate information and referrals to services, and engage with and motivate Helpline users to follow through on referrals. They will also receive training on Contact Center operations, supervision essentials, and addiction, screening, treatment services, and resources.

Benefits

HRiA offers strong benefits to its employees, including:

  • Competitive salaries
  • Health insurance
  • Retirement plan
  • Flexible summer hours
  • Vacation starting at four weeks
  • 13 paid holidays, and office closure at the end of December

Duties and Responsibilities

Management

  • Coordinate and implement projects related to contact center operations, including technology, equipment, onboarding & training, among others, as assigned.
  • Work with Helpline Management to coordinate Helpline staffing schedules to ensure continuous 24-hour staffing coverage.
  • Serve as liaison between SIS and other project and organizational teams, to ensure appropriate representation and facilitate team integration.
  • Supervise up to six SIS.
  • Participate in on-call rotation.

Project Work

  • Troubleshoot technical contact center issues, and serve as liaison to IT support.
  • Assist with coordination and implementation of onboarding and professional development activities.
  • Assess the needs of Helpline users by telephone, online chat, and SMS texting.
  • Provide appropriate information and referrals to substance use, problem gambling, and/or related services.
  • Engage and motivate Helpline users to follow through on referrals by using active listening and motivational interviewing techniques.
  • Obtain feedback on interactions with Helpline users.
  • Gather and record data from Helpline users in Helpline database.
  • Verify Helpline users’ insurance status, as applicable.
  • Escalate Helpline user interactions to Helpline Managers as needed.
  • Represent the Helpline at outreach events, meetings, and/or presentations as needed.

Thought Leadership

  • Continue to build and develop expertise in substance use disorders, problem gambling, and behavioral health equity.
  • Suggest ideas/improvements through participation in teams and committees.
  • Attend and actively participate in Helpline meetings and other activities to develop skills and make suggestions for project enhancements.

New Business Development

  • Maintain updated resume and bio for use in new business proposals.
  • Assist with technical components of new business proposals as needed.

Candidate Qualifications

  • Five years of related experience (lived or professional) in the fields of substance use, recovery, problem gambling, and/or harm reductions Services, and manage mentor bachelor’s degree in psychology, social work, human services, or related field in lieu of experience.
  • Certified Resource Specialist (through Inform USA) preferred or willingness to obtain certification (at HRiA expense) within one year of hire.
  • Demonstrated experience and ability to supervise staff, and provide appropriate guidance, feedback, mentorship, and support.
  • Experience in information and referral services, customer service, counseling, substance use, problem gambling, or human services required.
  • Ability to adapt to changes in work environment and expectations.
  • Customer/consumer focused with excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Good computer skills and experience and/or ability to use online systems and databases.
  • Openness to information that may be different from personal views.
  • Willingness to work with consumers who may be ambivalent, resistant, impaired or have psychological disorders.
  • Must be open to providing information about a variety of treatment options and paths to recovery based on a caller’s needs.
  • Must be respectful of cultural differences and value diversity of thought, backgrounds, and perspectives.
  • Must have high ethical standards and a willingness to comply with professional expectations.
  • Demonstrated history of dependability needed.
  • Two years of sobriety requested for people in recovery.
  • Fluency in a language other than English (e.g., Spanish, Portuguese, Mandarin) is a plus.

Hours for this position will be non-traditional, requiring either early morning or late evening and weekend availability. The position includes weekend or overnight on-call duties. The Helplines are open 24 hours/day, 7 days/week, 365 days a year.

This description is intended to indicate the kinds of work duties that will be required in this position. It is not intended to limit, or in any way modify, the rights of any supervisor to assign, direct, and contract work of staff under his/her supervision. The use of a particular illustration describing duties shall not be held to exclude other duties, not mentioned, that are of a similar level or difficulty.

Procedure for Candidacy

HRiA is actively seeking to build a diverse and experienced staff. The organization encourages multiple perspectives and experiences, supports a multicultural environment, and strives to hire and retain a diverse work force that reflects the populations we work with and the communities where we work. Diversity is a core value of HRiA resulting in culturally competent services, materials, resources, and programs. Our hiring and business practices appreciate the strengths offered through different backgrounds.

HRiA is an equal opportunity, affirmative action employer and is committed to providing access, equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or genetic information.

To apply, submit your cover letter and resume online at

Generally, our interviews take place between 9am-5pm ET. If you are contacted for an interview, please let us know if this timeframe is a challenge, so we can work with the interview team to find alternatives.

raw.description:
DATA ANALYST

Department: Finance and Administration

JOB SUMMARY

One More Child is seeking to employ a full-time Data Analyst to support its mission of impacting vulnerable children and struggling families through the collection, integration, analysis, forecasting, and visualization of organizational data. The Data Analyst will bridge the gap between raw data and actionable intelligence by leveraging Microsoft Fabric's unified analytics platform to transform data into strategic insights that improve decision-making across fundraising, finance, program operations, and organizational leadership.

This position will be responsible for analyzing data from multiple sources, developing semantic data models, identifying trends and opportunities, conducting predictive analysis, and delivering interactive Power BI dashboards that translate data into meaningful business insights. The ideal candidate will possess strong analytical skills, advanced Microsoft Fabric and Power BI expertise, and the ability to communicate complex data findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS

  • Design and maintain interactive dashboards, reports, and scorecards using Power BI
  • Monitor Fabric data pipelines and datasets and extend semantic models.
  • Perform trend analysis, forecasting, and predictive analytics to support organizational planning and decision-making.
  • Maintain reliable reporting systems that include data from multiple legacy organizational systems and new data systems as needed; identify inaccurate or inconsistent data and work with appropriate departments to cleanse data and resolve underlying issues.
  • Utilize SQL, Power BI, and Fabric analytics tools to identify insights, opportunities, risks, and performance trends.
  • Develop and support machine learning and predictive models using Microsoft Fabric Data Science tools, Spark and/or Python.
  • Maintain and respond to automated monitoring, alerts, and reporting solutions using Microsoft Fabric capabilities.
  • Collaborate with business stakeholders to define reporting requirements, KPIs, and analytical needs.
  • Develop report wireframes, mockups, or prototypes to validate layout, metrics, filters, and user experience prior to dashboard development.
  • Present data-driven recommendations and insights to leadership and department teams.
  • Support data governance, data quality, security, and reporting best practices across the organization.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • N/A


REQUIRED EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Information Systems, Computer Science, Statistics, Business Analytics, or a related field; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Three (3) or more years of experience in data analytics, business intelligence, reporting, or a related field.

raw.description:
Job Summary

The Head of Innovation leads the organization's innovation strategy, emerging-technology agenda, experimentation, and development of new products, services, business models, and operating approaches.

Within Insurance & Investments, the role identifies opportunities to use AI, automation, InsurTech, FinTech, data, digital platforms, and emerging technologies to improve customer experience, underwriting, claims, investment management, distribution, operational efficiency, and revenue growth.

The role acts as a bridge between business strategy, technology, digital transformation, product development, and external innovation ecosystems.

Key Responsibilities

Innovation Strategy

Develop and execute the enterprise innovation strategy and roadmap.

Establish innovation priorities aligned with corporate and business-unit objectives.

Identify emerging market, technology, customer, and business-model trends.

Build an innovation pipeline covering short-, medium-, and long-term opportunities.

Establish innovation governance, frameworks, KPIs, and investment criteria.

Develop business cases and ROI models for innovation initiatives.

Product & Business Model Innovation

Identify opportunities for new insurance and investment products.

Develop and test new digital products, services, and customer propositions.

Explore alternative distribution and revenue models.

Lead proof-of-concepts, pilots, MVPs, and commercialization programs.

Conduct market and competitor analysis.

Use customer insights to identify unmet needs and new opportunities.

Insurance Innovation

Focus areas may include:

AI-enabled underwriting

Automated claims processing

Digital claims journeys

Predictive risk assessment

Telematics and usage-based insurance

Embedded insurance

Digital distribution

InsurTech partnerships

Fraud detection

Automated customer service

Personalized insurance products

IoT-enabled risk monitoring

Investment & Wealth Innovation

Explore AI/analytics-enabled investment solutions.

Identify opportunities in digital wealth management.

Develop new investor engagement and self-service models.

Explore robo-advisory and personalized investment experiences.

Improve portfolio analytics and investor reporting.

Evaluate emerging investment technologies and fintech platforms.

Identify opportunities for alternative investment products and distribution models.

Emerging Technology

Evaluate and develop use cases involving:

Artificial Intelligence

Generative AI

Machine Learning

Automation / RPA

Blockchain / Distributed Ledger Technology

Cloud Computing

APIs

IoT

Advanced Analytics

Low-code / No-code

Digital Identity

Open Banking / Open Finance

FinTech / InsurTech platforms

Innovation Labs & Experimentation

Establish innovation labs, accelerators, or internal innovation programs.

Lead ideation workshops and design-thinking initiatives.

Develop prototypes and MVPs.

Test new technologies in controlled environments.

Establish criteria for scaling successful pilots.

Stop or redesign initiatives that do not demonstrate sufficient business value.

External Ecosystem & Partnerships

Build relationships with FinTechs, InsurTechs, startups, universities, technology providers, venture ecosystems, and research organizations.

Identify strategic partnerships and investment opportunities.

Evaluate startup technologies and potential strategic fit.

Manage innovation challenges, hackathons, accelerators, and partnerships.

Represent the organization at innovation and industry forums.

Data, AI & Digital Transformation

Partner with Data & Analytics teams on AI and advanced analytics opportunities.

Work with Digital and Technology leadership to scale successful innovations.

Identify automation opportunities across operations.

Promote data-driven experimentation and decision-making.

Ensure innovation initiatives complement the broader digital and technology roadmap.

Governance, Risk & Regulation

Ensure innovation initiatives comply with financial-services regulations.

Partner with Risk, Compliance, Legal, Information Security, and Data Privacy teams.

Establish responsible AI and technology governance.

Assess cybersecurity, privacy, operational, financial, and regulatory risks.

Establish appropriate controls for experimentation and production deployment.

Leadership & Commercialization

Build and lead innovation teams and cross-functional squads.

Manage innovation budgets and investment portfolios.

Establish innovation KPIs and executive reporting.

Track revenue, cost savings, customer impact, adoption, and ROI.

Develop commercialization plans for successful innovations.

Present innovation opportunities and results to executive leadership and the Board.

Ideal Candidate Profile

12–18+ years of experience across innovation, strategy, digital transformation, product, technology, consulting, or financial services.

5+ years in senior leadership roles.

Proven experience building and executing innovation strategies.

Strong understanding of emerging technologies and their commercial applications.

Experience with FinTech, InsurTech, AI, automation, digital products, analytics, or platform businesses.

Strong product-development and business-model innovation experience.

Experience taking concepts from ideation PoC MVP pilot commercialization.

Strong understanding of financial-services business models.

Experience working with startups, technology vendors, accelerators, or innovation ecosystems.

Excellent strategic thinking, commercial judgment, stakeholder management, and communication skills.

Bachelor's degree in Business, Technology, Engineering, Computer Science, Finance, or related field; MBA/master's preferred.

raw.description:
About the Role

Join a lean team at an early-stage AI-driven biotech company, working across computational protein design, experimental biology, and scientific software. You will help close the design-make-test-model loop, using experimental results to improve models and deliver more useful sequences.

What You'll Do

  • Refine discrete diffusion, protein language, and structure prediction models, including model architectures and constrained redesign workflows.

  • Operate and improve a scientific inference platform, and analyze user behavior, usage patterns, and churn.

  • Write, debug, and deploy protocols for liquid-handling robots and manage screening instrumentation.

  • Run BLI or SPR assays end-to-end, from assay design and sample preparation through kinetic fitting and quality control.

  • Diagnose experimental and computational failure modes, including mass transport, nonspecific binding, aggregation, and poor referencing.

  • Design sequences, synthesize or express them, measure kinetics, update models, and iterate on improved candidates.

  • Support scientific users and customer adoption with accurate, personalized outreach and an understanding of biotech buying processes.

What We're Looking For

  • At least 2 years building or operating protein design, protein language, or structure prediction systems in a design-make-test workflow.

  • At least 3 years in biotech or life sciences software go-to-market, solutions engineering, or customer success, including converting free users to paid offerings.

  • Hands-on experience writing production methods for Hamilton, Tecan, Opentrons, or equivalent liquid handlers.

  • Hands-on experience designing BLI or SPR assays, fitting kinetic curves, and troubleshooting assay results.

  • Practical experience with tools such as ESM, ProtT5, RFdiffusion, BindCraft, or equivalents, plus Python or similar scripting for automation and data analysis.

  • Biology, biochemistry, or life sciences knowledge, including protein structure, receptor biology, and scoring functions.

  • Experience with scientific software users, biotech sales cycles, peptide design, protein engineering, or drug discovery is valuable.

Compensation & Benefits

Consulting engagement compensation is $3,000 to $5,000 per month. Full-time conversion offers a base salary of $80,000 to $200,000 annually, depending on experience, plus equity. Visa sponsorship is not available.

Location

Hybrid, based in New York, United States, with increased on-site presence as internal screening operations launch.
